title: Stagewise tensor embeddings with integral image pass to a directed algebra colimit
statement: Let $R,C,B$ be commutative rings, $C,B$ commutative $R$-algebras, and $v:C\to B$ an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder and $(S_i,a_{ij})$ a diagram of commutative $R$-algebras with colimit $(S,a_i)$ in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Work in a common universe containing the index and all ring carriers. Give all tensor products their algebra multiplication $(s\otimes c)(s'\otimes c')=ss'\otimes cc'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $E_i=S_i\otimes_R C$, $D_i=S_i\otimes_R B$, $E=S\otimes_R C$, $D=S\otimes_R B$, and $f_i=1\otimes v:E_i\to D_i$, $f=1\otimes v:E\to D$. Assume every $f_i$ is injective and every element of its image is integral over $S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $f$ is injective and every element of its image is integral over $S$. In particular it restricts to an injective $S$-algebra map $q:E\to\overline S^{\,D}$, where $\overline S^{\,D}$ denotes the integral closure of $S$ in $D$, with $q(s\otimes c)=s\otimes v(c)$. For each $i\le j$ the maps satisfy $(a_{ij}\otimes1_B)f_i=f_j(a_{ij}\otimes1_C)$, and for each $i$ they satisfy $(a_i\otimes1_B)f_i=f(a_i\otimes1_C)$. No flatness, integrality or injectivity assumption on $v$, $S_i\to S_j$, or $S_i\to S$ is imposed beyond the displayed stagewise assumptions.

proof.text: Write $e_i=a_i\otimes1_C$, $d_i=a_i\otimes1_B$, and $e_{ij}=a_{ij}\otimes1_C$, $d_{ij}=a_{ij}\otimes1_B$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] defines these linear maps and $f_i,f$ by their pure-tensor formulas. They preserve multiplication: for example $f_i((s\otimes c)(t\otimes c\prime))=st\otimes v(cc\prime)=(s\otimes v(c))(t\otimes v(c\prime))$; bilinearity extends this equality to arbitrary finite sums. They preserve $1\otimes1$ and the scalar maps. On $s\otimes c$, both $d_{ij}f_i$ and $f_je_{ij}$ have value $a_{ij}(s)\otimes v(c)$; both $d_if_i$ and $fe_i$ have value $a_i(s)\otimes v(c)$. Generation by pure tensors proves both required identities.

proof.text: The nonempty directed preorder, viewed as a category, is filtered [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: a common upper bound receives two objects and there is at most one arrow between any pair. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] to the $R$-algebra diagram $(S_i)$ with $N=C$ and with $N=B$. Its universe hypothesis holds by the common-universe convention in the statement. Thus every $x\in E$ equals $e_i(x_i)$ for some $i,x_i\in E_i$; and $d_i(y_i)=0$ for $y_i\in D_i$ implies $d_{ij}(y_i)=0$ for some $j\ge i$. The maps $d_i$ are ring homomorphisms. These statements apply to the specified colimit cocone, by its unique cocone-compatible isomorphism with a chosen colimit.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; expanded using Tags 00D6, 00D7, 00DD, 00GI and 00GP.

proof.text: If $f(x)=0$, choose $x=e_i(x_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise]. Step 1 gives $d_i(f_i(x_i))=0$. The eventual-zero clause of that same node gives $j\ge i$ with $0=d_{ij}(f_i(x_i))=f_j(e_{ij}(x_i))$. Injectivity of $f_j$ gives $e_{ij}(x_i)=0$. Cocone compatibility gives $x=e_j(e_{ij}(x_i))=0$. Apply this kernel argument to $x-x\prime$ to obtain injectivity of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; expanded using Tags 00D6, 00D7, 00DD, 00GI and 00GP.

proof.text: For $x=e_i(x_i)$, stagewise integrality and [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] give $n\ge1$ and $r_0,\ldots,r_{n-1}\in S_i$ such that $y_i^n+\sum_{k<n}(r_k\otimes1_B)y_i^k=0$, where $y_i=f_i(x_i)$. Apply the ring map $d_i$ and use $d_i(y_i)=f(x)$ and $d_i(r_k\otimes1_B)=a_i(r_k)\otimes1_B$. The resulting equation $f(x)^n+\sum_{k<n}(a_i(r_k)\otimes1_B)f(x)^k=0$ is monic over $S$, so $f(x)$ is integral over $S$. This writes out preservation of a monic equation and needs no flatness or injectivity of a transition map.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; expanded using Tags 00D6, 00D7, 00DD, 00GI and 00GP.

proof.text: The integral elements form the $S$-subalgebra $\overline S^{\,D}\subseteq D$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Step 4 therefore defines $q(x)=f(x)$ with this restricted codomain. The ring and $S$-scalar laws follow from those for $f$ in Step 1. Equality of $q$-values implies equality of their images under the inclusion into $D$, hence equality of the inputs by Step 3. Finally $q(s\otimes c)=s\otimes v(c)$ follows from its defining formula.

lean.statement: theorem directed_integral_embedding (R C B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing C] [CommRing B] [Algebra R C] [Algebra R B] (v : C →ₐ[R] B) (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirectedOrder I] (F : I ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u, u} R) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (h_injective : ∀ i : I, Function.Injective (lTensor (S := R) (F.obj i) v)) (h_integral : ∀ (i : I) (x : (F.obj i : Type u) ⊗[R] C), IsIntegral (F.obj i) (lTensor (S := R) (F.obj i) v x)) : Function.Injective (lTensor (S := R) c.pt v) ∧ (∀ x : (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[R] C, IsIntegral c.pt (lTensor (S := R) c.pt v x)) ∧ (∃ q : (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[R] C →ₐ[c.pt] integralClosure c.pt ((c.pt : Type u) ⊗[R] B), Function.Injective q ∧ (∀ x : (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[R] C, (q x : (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[R] B) = lTensor (S := R) c.pt v x) ∧ (∀ (s : c.pt) (z : C), (q (s ⊗ₜ[R] z) : (c.pt : Type u) ⊗[R] B) = s ⊗ₜ[R] v z)) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), (rTensor B (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom).comp (lTensor (S := R) (F.obj i) v) = (lTensor (S := R) (F.obj j) v).comp (rTensor C (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom)) ∧ (∀ i : I, (rTensor B (c.ι.app i).hom).comp (lTensor (S := R) (F.obj i) v) = (lTensor (S := R) c.pt v).comp (rTensor C (c.ι.app i).hom))
